rendered: After cycling at 0.5C[1], the LLTO-2 coating retained the most capacity, at 86.2%[2] of its initial discharge capacity. The other LLTO coatings were LLTO-0.5 at 85.5%[3] and LLTO-1 at 57.2%[4]. The pristine NCM retained only 56.6%[5] of its initial discharge capacity after 200 cycles[6], so LLTO-2 and LLTO-0.5 far outperformed bare NCM, while LLTO-1 was only slightly above it. The text labels the rate-capability drop as coming from the 2 mol.% coating[7], and it does not explicitly tie that label to the LLTO-2 sample. The authors attribute the lower rate capability to a thicker coating layer, which they say suppresses electron transfer during charge and discharge.[8]
